description: Orbit Blue is a student team passionate about space and technology. We aim to build an interactive Martian Map using NASA data and visualization to make exploring Mars engaging and informative. We welcome teammates skilled in coding, web development, design, data analysis, AI/ML, and planetary science. Together, we hope to learn, innovate, and create a meaningful solution.
summary:
MarsWalk EVA by team Orbit_blue, is an interactive Mars mission-planning application developed to support safer and more informed astronaut exploration of the Martian surface. It provides an interactive map where users can explore Martian terrain, plan routes, select waypoints, examine potential hazards, and review mission-related information.

The project addresses the challenge of navigating unfamiliar and potentially dangerous Martian landscapes, where steep slopes, difficult terrain, and hard-to-reach scientific locations can make astronaut movement risky. By bringing map exploration, route planning, terrain-risk information, and mission context together in one platform, MarsWalk EVA helps users understand possible routes and make better-informed planning decisions.

This project is important because future human missions to Mars will require careful preparation to protect astronauts while allowing them to explore and conduct scientific research. MarsWalk EVA demonstrates how interactive mapping and digital planning tools could contribute to safer and more efficient surface exploration. It is a prototype for mission-planning support, not a certified astronaut navigation system.
details:
MarsWalk EVA – Interplanetary Tactical Mission Planner

MarsWalk EVA is an interactive Mars mission-planning application designed to support safer and more informed exploration of the Martian surface. It allows users to explore Mars through an interactive map, plan astronaut routes, select waypoints, examine terrain-related risks, and review mission information. The application focuses on the Gale Crater and Mount Sharp region.

The project addresses the challenges of navigating unfamiliar Martian terrain, including steep slopes, hazardous areas, and difficult-to-reach scientific locations. By combining map exploration, route planning, terrain information, and rover imagery in one platform, it helps users understand potential routes and make better-informed mission-planning decisions.

Its main benefits include improved visualization of Martian terrain, easier route comparison, identification of potential hazards, and better organization of mission information. The intended impact is to demonstrate how digital mapping and planning tools could contribute to safer and more efficient future human exploration of Mars.

We developed the project using **Python, FastAPI, JavaScript, Leaflet.js, GeoJSON, and Vercel**. FastAPI supports the backend, while Leaflet.js provides the interactive mapping interface.

The creative aspect of MarsWalk EVA is its combination of planetary mapping, route planning, waypoint inspection, and mission-related information in a single interactive experience. Instead of viewing terrain and mission information separately, users can explore them together.

During development, our team considered astronaut safety, terrain difficulty, accessibility of scientific locations, usability, technical feasibility, and the reliability of available planetary data. We also considered the limitations of a prototype and the need for further testing and validation before any real mission use.
